rektion: jdm. (Dat.) widerstreben; es widerstrebt jdm., etw. zu tun
meaning_en: to go against (someone's nature), to be repugnant to
definition_de: jemandem innerlich zuwider sein, sodass er etwas nicht tun möchte; Nomen: das Widerstreben (etw. nur mit Widerstreben tun)
example_de: Es widerstrebte ihm, den lebenden Hummer einfach ins kochende Wasser zu werfen.
example_en: It went against his grain to simply throw the live lobster into the boiling water.
visual_idea: Collocation 'es widerstrebt jdm., etw. zu tun': a man holds a live lobster at arm's length over a steaming pot, face turned away in a grimace. The inner resistance is visible in his body language, and the scene is memorable. The sentence shows the typical Dat. + zu-infinitive pattern.
image_prompt: a man in his thirties in a home kitchen holding a live dark blue lobster at arm's length above a large pot of boiling, steaming water, his body leaning back and his face turned away in a pained grimace, the lobster's claws raised, a lemon and herbs on the counter, warm evening kitchen light
negative_prompt: text, letters, watermark, signature, caption, blurry, extra fingers, deformed hands, cluttered background, multiple panels
video_prompt: in a home kitchen a man holds a live lobster at arm's length above a steaming pot, the lobster waves its claws, the man hesitates, leans back with a grimace, then slowly pulls the lobster back away from the pot; static medium shot
